title: Close indexed pose-application hot path and skeleton coverage gaps
description:
## User Mandate

> "Review this this external audit critically and synthesize into durable tasks as appropriate after cross-validating"

STRICT. Cross-validate the supplied animation and locomotion audit against current source and task records before accepting findings. Preserve audit provenance, do not reopen findings already fixed, and create only the durable task coverage required by confirmed mechanisms.

## Summary
Cross-validated residual work from `docs/audits/creaturecreator-animation-locomotion-deep-dive-2026-09-05-2029.md`. The current CC-069 adapter has a confirmed per-application allocation and string-keyed lookup path. A build-time terminal-bone rotation lookup and missing direct snapshot contract tests are also confirmed. The task owns these residuals without changing locomotion ownership.

## Scope
- Replace or bypass the per-call rotation dictionary in `PoseRotationResolver` with caller-owned or indexed rotation storage.
- Add an index-parallel `Transform[]` path in `CreatureRig` for `ApplyPose` while retaining the public stable-ID dictionary boundary.
- Replace `SkeletonInferrer.AppendLimbBones` terminal rotation `FindBone` lookup with the already computed previous rotation.
- Add focused tests for duplicate IDs, missing parents, bone-order mismatch, and invalid child indices in `SkeletonSnapshot`.
- Preserve the existing pure runtime and Unity adapter boundary. Do not implement locomotion, gait, terrain contact, or geometry binding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `CreatureRig.ApplyPose` performs no per-call managed dictionary allocation for rotations and no per-bone string-keyed lookup on the hot path.
- Existing rotation and pose behavior remains deterministic for terminal, segmented, branching, and coincident positions.
- `SkeletonInferrer` no longer performs a list scan to recover the terminal bone rotation.
- Focused runtime tests cover each listed `SkeletonSnapshot` contract and pass.
- A Unity or equivalent runtime test gate records the focused suite result. No task status changes to Done without executable validation.

## Validation
Run the focused runtime test suite for rig and pose application, plus the new snapshot contract tests. Run the runtime project build, `git diff --check`, and a performance-oriented allocation check or benchmark for repeated `ApplyPose` calls when the implementation is available.

## Findings
Source-confirmed from the supplied audit: C-1 and H-4. M-1 is accepted as a coverage addition. H-1, H-2, and H-3 were refuted as stale because current source and live records show TSK-0113, TSK-0114, and TSK-0116 complete. M-2 remains test organization, M-4 remains optional utility consolidation, and L-1 remains documentation drift.

## Blockers
No implementation blocker identified. Unity execution and a measured allocation result were unavailable during synthesis.

## Next Step
Implement the indexed pose-application path and focused contract tests under the CC-069 owner, then attach executable validation evidence.

comments.body: Synthesis evidence (2026-09-06 audit batch; see docs/audits/creaturecreator-audit-synthesis-2026-09-06-batch.md). second-order F-207 (P1): SkeletonSnapshot.HasSameBoneOrder only compares count + ordered IDs (SkeletonSnapshot.cs:191-199); it is used as the pose-compatibility gate in PoseRotationResolver (cs:33,62) but does not compare parent indices/IDs, SourcePartId, terminal/segment semantics, mirrored state, or rest pose/bind. Two snapshots with equal ordered IDs but different topology/bind would be accepted. Extend here (indexed pose hot path + skeleton compatibility). Downstream consumer TSK-0077 also relevant. F-208 (SkeletonSnapshot.Capture list-as-priority-queue readability, cs:109-123) is low-value; parent-before-child invariant already Done under TSK-0114 - optional. No duplicate task created.
